PullRequest.Title: sessions: polish cloud automation dialog and cards
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #341099, fixes #341100, fixes #341102, fixes #341104, fixes #341105, fixes #341117.

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Summary

Polishes the GitHub cloud automation dialog and repository labels on automation cards in the Agents window, based on test-plan feedback.

- **#341099:** Keep the allowed-tools button secondary, with a theme-aware border so it reads as clickable in light and dark themes.
- **#341100:** Start tool categories collapsed.
- **#341102:** Apply tool checkbox changes immediately to the dialog draft; Escape and Enter close the checklist without discarding changes. Show **All tools allowed**, **1 tool allowed**, or **N tools allowed** on the button. Creating or saving the automation still persists the draft.
- **#341104:** Remove the redundant tools description and update accessibility help to match the new selection behavior.
- **#341105:** Move the cloud execution note below the target controls; a target validation error replaces the note rather than appearing alongside it. Remove the create-mode “Define a prompt…” guidance per follow-up feedback; edit-mode guidance sits above the prompt.
- Restore breathing room above **New automation** and between the title and Name, while removing the hidden built-in message wrapper's unintended layout gap.
- **#341117:** Show only the repository name on cloud automation cards, preserving full owner/repo in the tooltip and accessible label.

Card changes are limited to repository labeling; Refresh and run-spinner work is not included.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed; refreshed client output before tests and the latest OSS reload.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\test\browser\automationDialog.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\automationsView.test.ts --reporter dot` — **238 passing**.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\quickinput\test\browser\quickinput.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\test\browser\automationDialog.test.ts --reporter dot` — **150 passing** after reverting the shared QuickTree fix.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Earlier live OSS validation covered the authenticated cloud dialog in light/dark themes, all/partial tools labels, collapsed categories, selection retained after Escape, and the card's repository label/tooltip. The final screenshot below is the accepted light-theme dialog with restored title spacing. The latest cloud replay was blocked by a sign-in/enablement error despite the account appearing signed in.

### Manual checks

1. In the Agents window, create a cloud automation for a private GitHub repository. Check the title spacing and the execution note beneath the target controls.
2. Open the tools checklist. Confirm collapsed categories, immediate checkbox updates, selection retained after Escape, and the all/partial/singular button labels.
3. Check the secondary tools button in light and dark themes.
4. Trigger a target validation error and confirm it replaces the execution note.
5. Check a cloud card: repository name only in the card, full owner/repo in its tooltip.

## Known follow-up

The shared QuickTree primary-button label can retain **Import** after cancelling Import Automation and then opening a tools tree. Ben accepted this as a nonblocking, separately scoped fix. The attempted QuickTree fix and its regression test were reverted, so this PR contains no shared QuickInput changes.

## Final screenshot

Accepted as-is. Hosted on an evidence-only branch, outside this PR's code diff.

![Final cloud automation dialog with restored title spacing and secondary All tools allowed button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode/88a782c50533994b251d3dba9795b039b9b853d8/final-cloud-dialog-restored-title-space.png)

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch targets in the cloud automation dialog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog and form render synchronously. Repository eligibility can resolve asynchronously after target selection; tool-catalog loading is asynchronous and the tools button remains disabled, so neither remote operation is newly placed on initial dialog-render progress by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected repository and query whether it is private.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one queued eligibility operation per uncached workspace key; cached selections reuse the observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same target-selection path performed the same cached and limited repository query before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected target remains pending until eligibility resolves, but dialog rendering can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the account's cloud automation tool catalog with listTools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful request per account-store lifetime; repeated calls while loading or after success are coalesced. A failed request occurs again only on explicit retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening a cloud configuration already invoked the same lazy, coalesced loadTools path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the dialog-open critical path; only configuring or saving unresolved default tool selection waits for the catalog.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected repository and one account-wide tool catalog per dialog; target eligibility is keyed by workspace and tool data is shared for the account lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository eligibility uses the existing targetEligibilityLimiter and keyed observable cache. Tool loading coalesces loading/ready states so repeated loadTools calls produce at most one in-flight request; the diff does not change either mechanism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Target eligibility reuses a per-workspace observable. Tools are loaded once per account lifetime, with ready/loading states suppressing duplicate requests and failures explicitly retryable. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed note placement and description access are local DOM/observable reads, while the transitive remote operations remain behind unchanged cached methods.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository and catalog latency vary by network and account, but their cardinality and scheduling are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the PR moves guidance in the DOM and removes a footer autorun without adding or multiplying remote work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle tools in the allowed-tools quick tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A checkbox event synchronously updates the quick tree, derives checked leaves, copies selected IDs, recomputes label/count state, and updates the underlying dialog button before the interaction completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective input is the number of tools in the loaded catalog plus unknown saved tool IDs. A leaf or category/check-all gesture emits one checked-leaf collection event after tree state changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely serialized on the UI thread and user-paced; there is no asynchronous fan-out or concurrent boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the already loaded account-wide catalog. No cache lookup, invalidation, or network retry is triggered by checkbox changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event implementation emits one checked-leaf array after each gesture, and the changed handler adds one flatMap plus updateToolsControls scans. There is no hidden boundary call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real catalog sizes are not established in the diff, but the added work is linear allocation/set construction over an already materialized, user-visible catalog and occurs once per user gesture.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added synchronous work is bounded by the visible catalog, user-paced, and lacks evidence of meaningful latency or jank at realistic cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type in or otherwise revalidate the automation form
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each prompt edit synchronously revalidates the form and updates validation DOM. The diff additionally reads the provider description and writes visibility/text for a single target note.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-size note update per revalidation event; frequency follows typing and target-control changes rather than collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI-thread work with no queue or parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider configuration is an in-memory observable/configuration object; reading its description performs no remote lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: prompt model changes call revalidate, which reaches showTargetValidationError, but the changed work is constant and does not force a geometry read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style/layout invalidation cost is environment-dependent, but only one short text node and its visibility/ARIA state are affected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: although the note is touched on a hot input path, the added constant one-node DOM work does not establish a concrete user-visible performance degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh and render automation cards in the Agents view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each catalogue render iterates automation descriptors and updates or reuses cards. The changed code derives the displayed repository basename before the existing conditional card update.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One substring/lastIndexOf operation per automation descriptor per render, scaling with card count and label length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, single-threaded card reconciliation. Existing provider refresh/polling is upstream and not initiated by the changed label derivation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent cards and latest descriptors are reused across renders. The diff neither changes those caches nor adds a cache miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: updateCard is reached once per existing card during render, and the changed expression has no transitive boundary or layout read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Automation counts and refresh frequency vary, but the added operation is a short in-memory string scan per card.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the per-card string operation is bounded and negligible relative to existing card reconciliation, with no new I/O, layout, or retained state.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The help provider constructs localized strings in memory and presents the accessible view; the diff only replaces static explanatory text.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed-size string for the cloud-dialog help section per help invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous fixed work; no parallelism or fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk is static localized content only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the string is fixed in source.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. Traced dialog rendering/revalidation, tool selection, repository/tool network paths, card refresh rendering, and accessibility help. The only new repeated work is bounded local DOM/string/collection processing; all network operations remain cached, coalesced, limited, and unchanged, so no actionable performance finding was submitted.
